annotations.keyFindings: Among 2,380 adults over four years, caries increment did not differ between risk-based and six-month recall (mean difference 0.1 surfaces); 41 percent of the risk-based group had intervals of 12 months or longer.
annotations.limitations: Trained practices in a trial; not a measure of routine practice.

annotations.keyFindings: In 12,000 records, 81 percent of adults had six-month recall regardless of recorded risk and the risk field was completed in 64 percent.
annotations.limitations: Cannot tell whether risk was assessed but not recorded.

annotations.keyFindings: Across 4,000 records, the risk field was blank in 29 percent and copied forward unchanged in 47 percent of repeat assessments.
annotations.limitations: Did not link risk to recall intervals.

annotations.keyFindings: Recommends adult intervals between 3 and 24 months set by risk at each examination; evidence judged of low certainty.
The 28 adults offered longer intervals mostly accepted them once reasons were explained, but some feared missed problems or losing their place.
annotations.limitations: One region; interviews after the offer.

annotations.keyFindings: In 38,500 adults, no recall interval was recorded for 19 percent in the most deprived quintile against 7 percent in the least deprived.
In 1,640 low-risk adults, caries increment at 12 to 24 months was similar to six-month recall (0.4 against 0.3 surfaces over three years).
annotations.limitations: Practices that adopted risk-based recall; 23 percent incomplete follow-up among movers.

annotations.keyFindings: Argues that activity-based contracts discourage longer intervals and proposes measuring interval distribution by recorded risk before contract change.

claims.text: In 12,000 records, 81 percent of adults had a six-month recall interval regardless of recorded risk, and the risk field was completed in 64 percent.
claims.passage: In all, 81 percent of adults had a six-month recall interval regardless of their recorded risk category, and the risk field was completed in 64 percent of records.
claims.interpretation: Risk-based recall may be rare in routine care; the local study measures it directly.

claims.text: The risk field was blank in 29 percent of records and copied forward unchanged in 47 percent of repeat assessments.
claims.passage: The risk field was blank in 29 percent of records.
claims.interpretation: Recorded risk is an imperfect reference; independent risk markers are needed.

claims.text: In a randomised trial, caries increment did not differ between risk-based and six-month recall over four years.
claims.passage: Caries increment did not differ between groups (mean difference 0.1 decayed, missing or filled surfaces).
claims.interpretation: Safety of longer intervals has randomised evidence already; the cohort option would largely repeat it.

claims.text: Adults in the most deprived quintile were more likely to have no recall interval recorded (19 percent against 7 percent).
claims.passage: Adults in the most deprived quintile were more likely to have no recall interval recorded (19 percent against 7 percent in the least deprived quintile).
claims.interpretation: Missing intervals must be analysed as a finding by deprivation, not excluded.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Randomised and cohort evidence suggests that longer intervals for low-risk adults do not increase decay, so the safety question has answers. Routine practice appears far from risk-based: in one large record study most adults had six-month recall whatever their recorded risk, risk fields are often blank or copied forward, and adults in deprived areas more often have no interval recorded. Patients accept longer intervals when reasons are explained. What is missing is a current measure of how intervals are set in this network, with recorded risk and independent risk markers, before contracts change.
gradeRationale: One randomised trial is indirect to routine practice; the practice-level evidence is observational and from other settings; one undated briefing.
summary: Eight retrieved records appraised; four claims; overall certainty low.
